answers.1: Yellow + Green — both are people-oriented, warm and relationship-focused, so they click socially (Red + Blue, being task-oriented, click on work instead).
answers.2: Red + Blue — both are task-focused: Red drives the result, Blue supplies the accuracy and structure.
answers.3: Red — the dominant, take-charge profile wants control and the lead role.
answers.4: Blue — precision, procedure, high standards and attention to detail (a Red streak helps with decisiveness under pressure).
answers.5: Yellow — loves the spotlight, an audience and talking.
answers.6: Blue — systematic, organized filing and record-keeping.
answers.7: Blue — needs data, analysis and verification before committing.
answers.8: Blue — punctuality is a rule and a matter of respect for the schedule (Green is also dependable, but Blue is clock-precise).
answers.9: Red — results matter more than rules; will cut corners to get it done.
answers.10: Red — pragmatic and risk-tolerant, will try anything that produces results faster (Yellow will try it for novelty's sake).
answers.11: Green — takes things personally, internalizes hurt and remembers it long after.
answers.12: Yellow — chaotic desk, but a huge network and knows exactly who/where to ask.
answers.13: Red — decisive, wants authority and hates waiting on others.
answers.14: Yellow — image-conscious, expressive, likes to be noticed.
answers.15: Red — thrives on challenge, competition and winning.
answers.16: Red — fast, blunt, snap judgments (Blue is the most critical, but slower and more analytical about it).
answers.17: All four together — a balanced Red/Yellow/Green/Blue team covers drive, enthusiasm, stability and accuracy; no single pair is best.
answers.18: Yellow — verbal, enthusiastic, thinks out loud.
answers.19: Yellow — quick, intuitive, open to novelty (Red grasps it fast too, but only the part useful for action).
answers.20: Red — delegates, then loses patience or trust and takes it back (Blue does the same out of perfectionism).
answers.22: Blue — reads and follows every step, including the last one.
answers.23: No single answer — it depends on you; people tend to gather others of their own or complementary profile, so this reveals your own color rather than a universal truth.
